chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Maruzi al-Maqarri narrated to us, saying: Abu Amr Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Maqarri al-Jarjani narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Mawsili in Baghdad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Asim al-Tarifi narrated to us, saying: Abu Zayd 'Abbas ibn Yazid ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Kahhal, the servant of Zayd ibn Ali, narrated to us, saying: My father Yazid ibn al-Husayn informed me, saying: Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to me, saying: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said:
Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'The Day when Allah will gather the Messengers and say: What were you responded with? They will say: We have no knowledge.'
He said: They will say: We have no knowledge of other than You.
He said: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: The Qur'an, all of it, is reproach, and its internal meaning is an approximation.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Messengers saying 'We have no knowledge' on the Day of Judgment according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the verse from Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:109) by interpreting the Messengers' declaration of 'no knowledge' as a negation of independent knowledge apart from God, thereby affirming divine omniscience. He further introduces the concept of *zahir* and *batin*, explaining that the Qur'an's outer text serves as a reproach to disbelievers while its inner essence brings believers closer to God. This dual function highlights the text's role in both warning and spiritual elevation, a key theme in Shia hermeneutics.
